source: MARKETING-TABLE.md, JSpark3 v2.0.1, reviewed 2026-10-04; rows 2, 4–9. Independently transcribed expectations; never generate from remeasured-data.ts.

groups.label: A complete program
groups.condition: fresh prompt: first streamed reasoning 0.26 s; first answer text by 0.62 s
groups.smallPrint: One request asked for a complete program, natural length (5,543 tokens), user-visible rate including first token
notes: Answer-text time is a collector upper bound.

groups.label: Short replies, fresh prompt
groups.condition: first token 0.31 s (code) / 0.25 s (prose) on a fresh prompt; 0.07‑0.08 s when the prompt is already cached
groups.smallPrint: Replies forced to 128 tokens (the llama-bench tg128 length)
notes: With the prompt already cached: code 108.5 tok/s, prose 73.5 tok/s.
One fresh-prompt and two cached-prompt requests each, for code and for prose.

groups.label: Long prose
groups.smallPrint: Replies forced to 2,000 tokens, thinking requested off, prompt already cached

groups.label: 32K-token prompt
groups.condition: read at ≈2,149 tok/s (estimated as prompt tokens ÷ client first-token time); the reply then streamed at 63 tok/s (after the first token)
notes: End to end, counting the 15.3 s before the first token: 18.5 tok/s.

groups.chartSmallPrint: One request, unique prompt (no cache), 400-token reply
groups.label: 64K-token prompt
groups.condition: read at ≈2,102 tok/s (the same estimate); the reply then streamed at 71 tok/s (after the first token)
notes: End to end, counting the 31.2 s before the first token: 10.9 tok/s.

groups.chartSmallPrint: Separate requests in one session chain: 112,728 / 112,743 prompt tokens; the disk request reused 112,156 tokens. Different system prefix and output limit, so an illustrative disk-hit vs fresh-prefill observation, not an identical-request A/B. Disk save needs idle time; back-to-back large-session traffic can prevent it (known issue 17)
groups.label: Server prefill
notes: Seen from the client, the first reasoning arrived at 2.5 s with the disk cache and at 56.9 s fresh.

groups.chartSmallPrint: Replies of 400 tokens started together, thinking requested off, temperature 0. Combined rate = tokens after each first token ÷ time from the earliest first token to the latest last token, the same formula as v1.8's ladder, which used 512-token replies. Measured 2026-10-03
groups.label: Prose, one stream
groups.smallPrint: Prompt cache: v1.8 fresh, v2.0.1 cached. At one stream the rate is timed from the first token, so the cache doesn't enter it (v2.0.1 one-stream code measured 107.7 fresh vs 107.8 cached).
notes: Grey figure is v1.8.0's published ladder, better of 2 runs, unscreened for repetition.
